The range display is a group named rangeLabel whose two range fields are buttons named startLabel and endLabel with their times, each exposing whether it is the one being set; no word for start or end is drawn, so these names are what tells assistive technology which is which. The hour and minute wheels and selectors are spin buttons named by hourLabel and minuteLabel, whose values are read as drawn (the hour with its period in a 12-hour clock), and they stay spin buttons while a number is typed into them. The period is a third spin button beside them, named periodLabel, whose value is the locale's name for before or after noon. The dial is a pointer surface hidden from assistive technology: everything it does, the selectors do too.
notes: The selectors, the period selector and the range fields are at least the minimum target in both dimensions and a wheel's rows at least the target's height (DTM-32); the dial is larger than the target. The calendar's cells, the tabs and the Buttons meet the target themselves (CAL-1, TAB-5, BTN-5).

Focus: a modal picker is a modal overlay — it keeps focus in and draws a scrim. A docked picker is an operated overlay that is not modal: it takes focus and returns it to its anchor, but Tab leaves it and closes it.

Typing a whole date or time is still the Text field's job (a trailing icon-only Button opens this picker), with its own reading rules for a date in the locale's order. Here a wheel takes only its own number: a press on its chosen value, or a digit on a keyboard, types the hour or the minute (DTM-43 to DTM-45), so a person who types reaches a time in three or four keys, and a person who does not still reaches every value by the arrow keys, by dragging and by assistive technology's increment and decrement.

The two ends of a range are not tabs: tabs say one of several views, and the two ends are two values that are both always shown. They are two buttons in a named group, each read with its name, its time and whether it is the one being set ("Start, 9:00 AM, selected"). The dash between them is decoration and is hidden; the names carry what the dash and the order show.
The entry-mode tabs draw glyphs alone. Their accessible names are wheelsLabel and dialLabel, so a screen reader reads "Wheels, tab, 1 of 2"; both words are the product's.
Escape ends a typed entry before it closes the picker, as it ends any edit inside a dialog first: one press never both discards a number and dismisses the surface.

The period is not tabs: tabs say that what is below them is one of several views, and AM or PM is a part of one value. It is exposed as the third field of a time, as the AM/PM field of a native time input is: a spin button of two values named periodLabel ("Period, PM"), which Up and Down Arrow, a press, and assistive technology's increment and decrement change. The hour's own value repeats the period ("7 PM"), so a person who never reaches the period control still hears which half of the day is set.

The dial mode's period selector shows the pending period alone and changes to the other when pressed. It is one target the height of the selectors: two names stacked in that height would be two targets shorter than the minimum, each over the other's edge (DTM-32). In the wheels mode both names are in view, as every value of a wheel's neighbourhood is.

The picker has no words of its own. Month, weekday and period names, digits and date and time forms are the platform's locale data, in the locale the picker was given. Every other word it shows or announces is the product's: a prop of this instance, or the product's words set once. Its name, label, is this instance's alone.

The web exposes each wheel and selector with role spinbutton, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext, a wheel on an input whose inputmode is numeric so that a touch keyboard is the number pad, and each range field as a button with aria-pressed in a role group; SwiftUI with the adjustable trait (accessibilityAdjustableAction) and a number-pad text field for an entry; Compose with progressBarRangeInfo and setProgress semantics and KeyboardType.Number; Flutter with Semantics increasedValue, decreasedValue, onIncrease and onDecrease and TextInputType.number; React Native with the adjustable role, the increment and decrement actions and a number-pad TextInput.

Text size: at 200% the wheels, the selectors and the dial's numbers grow; a modal picker scrolls between its header and its actions when the window is short (DTM-36), and the horizontal layout keeps a phone held sideways usable.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

A time outside min and max keeps its place on the wheels and the dial, drawn faded, and is passed over: a wheel settles on the nearest available row, the arrow keys go on to the next available value, and the dial takes the available value nearest the pointer, as the out-of-range values of a native time picker are dimmed and not chosen. Assistive technology never hears one as a spin button's value: each spin button's minimum and maximum are its first and last available values. Leaving them out instead would move every value after them, so that the place a person knows a time by (12 at the top of the dial, the next hour below this one) would change with the bounds.

web.name: tanrei-date-time-picker
web.notes: Attributes are kebab-case (`disabled-dates` is a space-separated list of ISO dates, `first-day-of-week`, `start-view`, `show-adjacent-days`, `hour-cycle`, `minute-step`, `entry-mode`, `wheels-label`, …); `isDateDisabled` is a property only. `entryMode` is not HTML's global `inputmode`. `value`, `start` and `end` are the strings of `<input type=date>`, `type=time` and `type=datetime-local`, set before `change` fires; `close` is a CustomEvent whose `detail.reason` is the reason. A modal picker is a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` in the shadow root, with `::backdrop` as the scrim; its `cancel` becomes close with `escape` when an Escape key caused it, and with `back` otherwise. A docked picker takes `anchor` and `opener` (element ids), sets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` on the opener, and is a manual popover in the top layer with its own light dismiss so that close carries its reason. Inside the shadow root: a `<tanrei-calendar>`; one `<tanrei-tabs variant="secondary">` row, the entry-mode tabs, which hugs and whose two `<tanrei-tab>`s are `label-hidden` with `icon="keyboard"` and `icon="schedule"`, and whose panel is the time section; the period as an element with role spinbutton (`aria-valuemin="1"`, `aria-valuemax="2"`, `aria-valuenow` and the period's name as `aria-valuetext`), `part="period"` — a third wheel of two rows that does not loop in the wheels mode, a button-like cell in the time display in the dial mode — placed before the hour when `formatToParts` gives the `dayPeriod` part before the `hour` part; the range display as a `role="group"` with two `<button part="range-field" aria-pressed>` and an `aria-hidden` dash, in a grid with two equal columns that fills the time section's inline size (and both columns of the horizontal layout of mode time); wheels and selectors as elements with role spinbutton, a wheel's middle row being an `<input inputmode="numeric" role="spinbutton">` that is read-only until a typed entry begins (a tap that ends without a drag, or a digit key), so that a drag raises no keyboard; the dial drawn with pointer events and `aria-hidden`; Cancel and OK as `<tanrei-button>`s placed by the button group's placement code, with the variant read from the resolved comp.date-time-picker.actions.variant. The entry modes offered are read from the resolved comp.date-time-picker.time.entry-modes once per system. Locale data from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (`formatToParts` with `hour12` for the period names and the separator; `resolvedOptions().hourCycle` for the preferred clock); without `locale` it reads the nearest `lang` attribute, then `navigator.language`. It uses the package's locale helpers, overlay placement and dial (`clock.ts`). A value outside `min` and `max` (DTM-50) is a wheel row or a dial number with `data-unavailable`, faded by `opacity`; a spin button's `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are its first and last available values. The `inline` attribute, for tests, draws the open surface in place (DTM-1's verify). Words: the element has no words of its own. A words attribute (`confirm-label`, `cancel-label`, `hour-label` and the others) left empty read the product's words, set once with `setWords()` from `@tanrei/web`; the element draws again when they change. Where neither the instance nor the product gives them, the hour's, the minute's and the period's names are `Intl.DisplayNames(locale, { type: 'dateTimeField' })` (`hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod`) and the present day's word is `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`'s for day 0.

swiftui.name: tanreiDateTimePicker
swiftui.notes: Planned. A view modifier, as `.sheet` and `.popover` are: `.tanreiDateTimePicker(isPresented:, selection: Binding<DateComponents?>, mode:, presentation:, …)` for one value and `.tanreiDateTimePicker(isPresented:, range: Binding<TanreiDateTimeRange>, mode:, …)` for a span, where `TanreiDateTimeRange` holds `start` and `end` as `DateComponents?`; the overload is range, and `mode` chooses which components are read and written (year, month and day; hour and minute; or both), so no time zone enters. Writing the binding is change; the picker writes false to `isPresented` itself and calls `onClose` with the reason. The words are fields of a `TanreiDateTimePickerLabels` passed as `labels:`, whose field names are the spec's. `locale` defaults to the `\.locale` environment; the preferred clock comes from `DateFormatter.dateFormat(fromTemplate: "j", …)`. Modal: `.fullScreenCover` with a clear background and the system transition off, as the dialog. Docked: drawn in its anchor's overlay and placed by Tanrei. The calendar is `TanreiCalendar`, the entry-mode tabs `TanreiTabs` (each with a glyph and `labelStyle: .iconOnly`), the period one view with `.accessibilityAdjustableAction` and `.accessibilityValue` (a third wheel in the wheels mode, a pressable cell in the dial mode), the range fields two `Button`s with the `.isSelected` trait in an accessibility container, a typed entry a hidden `TextField` with `.keyboardType(.numberPad)` on iOS and `.onKeyPress` for digits elsewhere, the actions `TanreiButton`s; the wheels are Tanrei's own (a scroll view with `.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)` per wheel) with `.accessibilityAdjustableAction`, not the system's wheel picker, whose look no token reaches. Snapshot harness: `TanreiDateTimePickerSurface` drawn in place on the fixture's stage. The product's words are read from the `\.tanreiWords` environment value.

compose.name: TanreiDateTimePicker
compose.notes: Planned. `TanreiDateTimePicker(visible, onClose, presentation, mode, range, value, start, end, onChange, min, max, disabledDates, isDateDisabled, today, firstDayOfWeek, locale, startView, showAdjacentDays, hourCycle, minuteStep, entryMode, unit, layout, labels)`. Values are `TanreiDateTime(date: TanreiDate?, time: TanreiTime?)`, of which `mode` says which half is read (API 23 has no `java.time`); `onChange` receives a `TanreiDateTimeSelection(value, start, end)`; the caller keeps the state (hoisting) and sets `visible` to false from `onClose`, which carries the reason. The words, `label` among them, are fields of a `TanreiDateTimePickerLabels`. Modal: a `Dialog` window with the platform width and dim off, as `TanreiDialog`. Docked: a `Popup` inside the anchor's `Box`, as `TanreiMenu`. The calendar is `TanreiCalendar`, the entry-mode tabs `TanreiTabs` (icon-only), the period one node with `progressBarRangeInfo` over two steps, `stateDescription` for its name and `setProgress` (a third wheel in the wheels mode, a clickable cell in the dial mode), the range fields two boxes with `Role.Button` and `selected` semantics, a typed entry a `BasicTextField` with `KeyboardType.Number` behind the wheel's middle row and `onPreviewKeyEvent` for digits, the actions `TanreiButton`s; each wheel is a `LazyColumn` with snapping fling and `progressBarRangeInfo` / `setProgress` semantics; the dial is `pointerInput` with `clearAndSetSemantics {}`. Snapshot harness: `TanreiDateTimePickerContent` drawn in place on the fixture's stage. The product's words are read from `LocalTanreiWords`.

flutter.name: TanreiDateTimePicker
flutter.notes: Planned. Flutter's idiom, as its own date and time pickers: a modal picker is `showTanreiDateTimePicker(context:, mode:, range:, value:, start:, end:, firstDate:, lastDate:, …)`, which pushes a modal route that draws the scrim as its barrier and returns a `Future<TanreiDateTimeSelection?>`, completed with the committed choice on OK and with null otherwise; `onChanged` and `onClose` are also called, in that order. A docked picker is `TanreiDateTimePickerAnchor(controller:, builder:, …)`, shaped like the menu's anchor and shown in the `Overlay`. `firstDate`, `lastDate` and `currentDate` keep Flutter's names. Values are `DateTime`s of which only the parts `mode` names are read. Month, weekday and period names, date forms, the separator and the preferred clock come from `TanreiDateLocalizations` (English built in, no `intl` dependency), and `MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormatOf` wins for hourCycle locale. The calendar is `TanreiCalendar`, the entry-mode tabs `TanreiTabBar` (icon-only), the period one widget under `Semantics` with `value`, `increasedValue`, `decreasedValue`, `onIncrease` and `onDecrease` (a third wheel that does not loop in the wheels mode, a pressable cell in the dial mode), the range fields two widgets under `Semantics(button: true, selected:)`, a typed entry an `EditableText` with `TextInputType.number` behind the wheel's middle row and a `Focus` `onKeyEvent` for digits, the actions `TanreiButton`s; each wheel is a `ListWheelScrollView.useDelegate` with a looping child delegate and a `FixedExtentScrollPhysics`, under `Semantics` with `increasedValue`, `decreasedValue`, `onIncrease` and `onDecrease`. Snapshot harness: a golden of the whole stage after `showTanreiDateTimePicker` (modal), or of `TanreiDateTimePicker` drawn in place (docked). The product's words are read from the `TanreiWords` inherited widget, which the app fills from its own localizations.

react-native.name: DateTimePicker
react-native.notes: Planned. Controlled: `visible`, `onClose({ reason })` and `onChange({ value, start, end })`, the values being the mode's ISO strings, never `Date` objects; the caller moves them and sets `visible` to false. A product that also uses the community package of the same name imports this one under another name. A modal picker is presented in a transparent `Modal` with `animationType="none"`, `statusBarTranslucent` and `navigationBarTranslucent`, as the dialog; a docked picker takes `anchorRef` and is drawn on the overlay layer that `TanreiProvider` renders, placed by measuring the anchor, with Android's back (`BackHandler`) as close. Locale data from Hermes's `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. Snapshot harness: `DateTimePickerSurface` drawn in place on the fixture's stage. The product's words are read from the `TanreiWordsProvider` context.
